concepts.def: Giving 2.5% of savings to charity yearly.
Fasting from dawn to sunset during Ramadan.
Ninth month of the Islamic calendar.

walkthroughs.body_html: Zakah is the third Pillar. Muslims who can afford it give 2.5% of their savings each year to the poor and to good causes. It reminds Muslims that all wealth comes from God and should be shared.

Sawm is the fourth Pillar — fasting during Ramadan, the ninth month of the Islamic calendar. From dawn to sunset, Muslims do not eat, drink, smoke or argue. Fasting builds self-discipline and reminds Muslims of those who are hungry.
During Ramadan, Muslims wake before dawn for suhoor (early meal) and break the fast at sunset with iftar, often starting with dates and water. Ramadan ends with the celebration of Eid al-Fitr.
